data.title: Hwang In-beom calls for stability as South Korea faces Qatar
data.content:
Midfielder Hwang In-beom speaks to reporters before a training session at Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium in Doha on Nov. 16.

 

YONHAP

Veteran midfielder Hwang In-beom said Monday that having a caretaker boss is far from ideal for the national team, and that he would like more stability on the bench.

Hwang and the Korean team will play their sixth and likely final match under interim manager Robert Moreno on Tuesday against Qatar in Doha. [...] The interim coach plans to test young players against Qatar as his future remains uncertain following the Asian Cup’s postponement.
 

  #### Once a source of national pride, Korean football is losing form both on and off the pitch

  Falling fan support, an ongoing leadership vacuum and FIFA concerns over election reforms have left Korea's national team at a crossroads.
 

  #### Taeguk Warriors look to close out tumultuous year with win against host Qatar [...] The KFA chose to sign Moreno on a six-match contract that will take him through Nov. 27, instead of rushing to hire a full-time coach while its presidency remained vacant. Moreno is the third caretaker manager for the Taegeuk Warriors in the past two-and-a-half years, following Hwang Sun-hong and Kim Do-hoon, who had stepped in after Jurgen Klinsmann got sacked in early 2024.
